title: Kyle Schwarber pops 2 homers into the corn during MLB’s Field of Dreams game
content:
MLB’s Field of Dreams game returned Thursday, as the Philadelphia Phillies met the Minnesota Twins for a unique showcase of the sport in the cornfields of Iowa. And it did not take long for Philadelphia slugger Kyle Schwarber to make an impact.

Schwarber sent the third pitch he saw — a 95.4 mph fastball from Twins right-hander Taj Bradley — beyond the right-field fence and into the corn.

His leadoff home run came not long after a poignant start to the night, which saw several members of the Baseball Hall of Fame emerge from the cornfield shortly before the game.

It all marked a rather dramatic beginning for the Field of Dreams game, which returned to Dyersville, Iowa, this summer after a yearslong hiatus. The event, staged at the site of the 1989 film, debuted in 2021 and was held the following year, but it was paused amid renovation work at the complex.

Schwarber wasn’t done after that homer in the first. He took Bradley deep again in the fourth inning, when he sent the ball to right with a 39-degree launch angle. Even in the Iowa wind, Schwarber’s blast had enough juice to reach the wall. The ball ricocheted off Luke Keaschall’s glove into the corn.

The 33-year-old Schwarber, the runner-up in this summer’s Home Run Derby, now has an MLB-leading 37 homers this season.
